title: CLAY CITY SCHOOL BOARD MEETS
full_story:
The Clay City School Board met Tuesday evening and were able to constitute a quorum after failing to do so at Thursday’s regular meeting date.

Board President Misty Lindeman called the meeting to order and members quickly approved the meeting agenda and past meeting minutes.

Superintendent John Neubaum went over the financial report, noting that the transportation payments to the district have been much lower than anticipated.  He also noted the payments for electricity have been very high and he is looking at ways the district may be able to lower costs.  The board then approved the financial report as presented.

Supt. Neubaum then delved into informational items beginning with the upcoming annual audit prepared by Kemper CPA Group.  He said the report was originally expected in November but indicated it may not come until December.  Neubaum stated that the county is forming plans to deal with emergency situations such as natural disasters.  As part of the process, grant money may become available from the federal government and school districts are asked to come up with a wish list of items that would help deal with the aftermath of storm damage.  He also spoke about rising health insurance rates.  He said right now Blue Cross/Blue Shield has a cap rate of 14.5% for one more year.  But the district also has a 200% loss ratio following the school bus accident last year.  And without that cap, insurance rates would skyrocket.  During this process, it was learned Blue Cross/Blue Shield charged 16.8% and have since issued a refund for the overcharge.  He did believe however that the district may seek another option, perhaps offering HSA’s (Health Savings Accounts) for employees.  Other items included announcing the Veterans Day Assembly on November 9th, which will include Kindergarten students leading the Pledge of Allegiance and the school band performing for students and veterans.  Supt. Neubaum brought up the topic of the tax levy and asked board member Amanda Noll to investigate the matter and he announced the Triple-I convention is quickly approaching with Dusty Thompson scheduled to attend and he invited other members to also attend if they wanted.

In the Principal’s Report, Brian Wattles reported Pre-K students visited a pumpkin patch earlier in the day and First Graders are looking forward to a field trip to the Clay City Firehouse.  Fourth and Fifth Grade Students are working on art projects at home to carve a pumpkin and enter it for judging in the Halloween contest.  Fifth Graders are also working on science experiments.  Sixth Grade students attended tech fest with Mrs. Walker and Mrs. Billingsley completed First Quarter with a Pizza Party.  Student Council is sponsoring Red Ribbon Week October 26-30 for elementary and junior high students. The Halloween Parade/Costume Contest is October 30th.  National Honor Society took a college tour field trip to EIU.  Band students plan to march in the upcoming Louisville Fall Harvest Festival Parade on October 31st.  LouEllen Harvel was selected to play in the District 5 ILME Senior Band and perform at EIU with other students from the southern part of the state in a large music festival.  Mrs. Collins hosted a FAFSA night for seniors.  And October 16th is the end of the first quarter.  The High School Scholastic Bowl team begins their season with a first match November 2nd, and a tournament in Robinson on November 7th.  Also 8th grade continues to test their Bunsen burner skills in the lab.

Members then went into closed session.  When the board returned, they voted to uphold student discipline as presented and then adjourned.

title: DRIVER IDENTIFIED
full_story:
The Illinois State Police released the name of the driver involved in a fatal crash last month that claimed the life of a local Amish teacher.  Loree Teague, 20 of Flora was driving an SUV on Wayne County Highway 16 when her vehicle crashed into the back of an Amish buggy.  The accident happened shortly after 7:49 am on September 29th.

The accident claimed the life of Rebecca Esh, a teacher in the Amish community.  The victim was pronounced dead at the scene.  The horse pulling the buggy sustained major injuries and was put down at the scene.

Illinois State Police issued Teague a citation for failure to reduce speed to avoid an accident.  The citation was recorded in the Wayne County Circuit Clerk’s office on Tuesday, October 13th.  A first appearance for Teague has been set for November 3rd.

title: FLORA HALLOWEEN PARADE
full_story:
Entry forms for the Flora Chamber of Commerce Halloween Parade on Saturday night, October 31st at 7:00 pm are now available.  There is no theme, so entrants can use their own creativity when planning the entry.  All entries to the parade must be registered with the Chamber in order to participate.  Please register at the chamber no later than Noon on Friday, October 30th.  The Chamber office is open on Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday from 8 am to 5 pm.

The parade route will start at The Depot (State Street) and end at Christ Church (Olive Street).  Emergency vehicles will be allowed to sound their sirens during the parade.

Staging areas will be given the day you register and parade numbers will be given the day of the parade when you check in.  Location of your Staging Area will be based on the type of entry.  The Chamber is asking everyone to please be respectful of the staging areas and leave them in the same condition they were in upon arrival.  All entries must check in with the staging area volunteer in the brightly colored vest, to officially check in and verify the entry has their card number on their entry for judging.  Bands, queens, and political entries do not need parade cards but do need to check in with the stage volunteer.

Horses are to unload at the Price Less IGA at 6 pm with a mandatory police escort to the grass area of GSI beginning at 6:15.  If you miss the police escort you will not be permitted in the parade.

Handicap spectators may park at Southern Lumber Company (corner of E. North Ave & South Mill) and please use the south entrance closest to the tracks.

All entries are required to register.  A $10 late fee will be required by any unregistered participant if they register after Noon on Friday, October 30th.  There will be absolutely no throwing of candy from vehicles or trailers/float, candy can be handed out or tossed if you are a walker on the sides of the street.  If an entry is caught throwing, they will be disqualified from judging.

Performance groups may stop at the judging stand and do a performance no longer than 90 seconds.  Any performance longer than 90 seconds will disqualify you from judging.

Arriel Dulaney, executive director of the Flora Chamber of Commerce will be discussing the parade today on the ReVue at 2 pm.

title: JURY TRIAL SET
full_story:
Stacey R. Robbins, 47, of rural Fairfield accused of faking cancer for a profit is now set to go to trial.

She previously pleaded not guilty to a charge of theft, a Class-2 felony and deceptive practice, a Class-4 felony.

A jury trial is set for April 13th, which is two years after the alleged crimes happened.

Court documents show she was an employee of the Fairfield Grade school.  Robbins collected cash from a number of individual donors and through various school fundraisers and various fundraisers at the Roads Church near Norris City.  In the deceptive practice case, Robbins is accused of taking more than $7,000 from a GoFundMe page that a friend set up.

Officials say the money was for treatments Robbins didn’t need, but she kept the money.  Several victims are listed in court documents.

title: NTSB TRAIN DERAILMENT REPORT
full_story:
The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) issued its final report on the July 2025 Norfolk-Southern train derailment near the town of Browns in Edwards County.

The report indicated that the incident occurred at 5:45 pm on July 18th along track in the railroad’s Southern West Subdivision.  24 cars of an eastbound freight train derailed while passing over a spring switch.  The derailed cars struck a westbound train that was stopped on an adjacent track.

Three tank cars carrying hazardous materials were breached, releasing molten sulfur and ethanol.  Two crew members aboard the stopped train were injured after jumping from a locomotive just before it was impacted by a derailed tank car.

Following the incident, Norfolk-Southern inspected all 205 of its mainline spring switches along its routes and revised its maintenance policies in regard to work performed on those switches.

title: I64 I57 CLOSURE
full_story:
The Illinois Department of Transportation announced that Interstate 64 eastbound at US 51 in Jefferson County will be closed from 10 pm Thursday, to 6 am Friday, for overnight maintenance work.

Eastbound I-64 traffic will be detoured south on US 51 to Illinois 15, then east on Illinois 15 to I-57/I-64 in Mount Vernon.

During the same overnight work period, the southbound driving lane of I-57 will be closed just south of the I-57/I-64 merge.

Motorists should expect delays and allow additional time for their commutes.  Drivers are urged to reduce speed, remain alert for changing conditions, obey all construction signage and refrain from using mobile devices while approaching and traveling through the work zone.

The work is expected to be completed by 6 am Friday, weather permitting.

title: IDNR TO PAUSE CWD MEETINGS
full_story:
The Illinois Department of Natural Resources (IDNR) will temporarily pause public meetings throughout northern and west-central Illinois this fall to prepare materials outlining changes to the state’s chronic wasting disease (CWD) program goals, objectives and future disease surveillance strategies.

The department is refining its CWD management strategy following its decision in spring 2026 to discontinue targeted deer removal, also known as sharpshooting, statewide.

IDNR staff will resume public meetings in fall 2027 to discuss the future direction of the CWD program and answer questions about the disease, as CWD remains an important issue and will continue to be a priority in future deer management discussions in Illinois.  Landowners, hunters and other concerned citizens are encouraged to attend.

Beginning in fall 2026, IDNR will offer voluntary mail-in sampling kits for hunters who want to collect lymph nodes from adult deer for CWD testing.  Kits will be available on a first-come, first-served basis while supplies last.  Hunters may request up to two kits at a time and can request additional kits as needed if they harvest more deer.  Hunters can request mail-in sampling kits online or by contacting their local district wildlife biologist.

CWD is a fatal disease of the central nervous system that affects deer and elk.  The disease was first detected in Illinois in 2002 in a suspect adult female deer from northwestern Boone County.  Since then, 199,136 wild deer have been sampled statewide, and 3,410 deer have tested positive for CWD.  The disease has been detected in 28 counties across northern and central Illinois.

From July 1, 2025, through June 30, 2026, IDNR identified 662 CWD-positive deer in 28 Illinois counties.  Annual CWD reports are available online.

For more information about the meetings or CWD, contact Chris Jacques, IDNR wildlife disease program manager, at [email protected].
